EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by bands typical of a para-disubstituted benzene: 1) an intense ring-breathing mode at 998 cm⁻¹, 2) strong C–H out-of-plane deformation near 834 cm⁻¹, and 3) characteristic aromatic C=C stretches at 1588 cm⁻¹ and 1526 cm⁻¹. O-alkyl-substituted benzenes show a strong C–O stretch around 1040–1060 cm⁻¹ (observed at 1049 cm⁻¹). Additional medium bands at 1286–1311, 1399 and 1446 cm⁻¹ match typical in-plane C–H bends and CH₃ deformations of methoxy-substituted aromatics, while C–Cl/S–C bends can account for the 621–699 cm⁻¹ region. The high-frequency C–H stretches at 2956 and 3073 cm⁻¹ are also consistent with alkyl and aromatic C–H bonds. Among the candidates, only molecule 1 (COCSc1ccc(Cl)cc1) is a para-disubstituted benzene bearing both a methoxy (–OCH₃, giving the 1049 cm⁻¹ band) and a chloro substituent (supporting the 620–700 cm⁻¹ region), as well as a thioether linkage accounting for additional C–S modes. No other candidate possesses this combination of structural features or can rationalize the dominant 998/834 cm⁻¹ para-disubstituted benzene pattern. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the observed Raman peaks.
